findings.description: The generated profile's Models section still says a relaunch or respawn after a CI fix round climbs one rung. This PR makes that false: a first CI fix round now keeps its rung.
findings.body:
**Stale climb rule in the conductor's generated profile.** This PR rewrote the CI-fix-round rule in `skills/pup/SKILL.md`, `src/claude/model-ladder.constants.ts` and ADR 0092. One copy was missed. `conductorModelsSection` still tells the conductor:

```ts
'relaunch or respawn after a gate rejection, a CI fix round, a stall or a dead turn ' +
'climbs one rung. A blocked task never climbs. ' +
```

Under this PR, `fixRoundFailure` returns `undefined` for a first round, so that round stays on its rung. Only a later round climbs, as `repeat-fix-round`. A re-gate from `merged` to `merged` is also no longer a window failure. The conductor is the agent that decides on `pup fix` and relaunches, so its profile now describes the old rule. The text is not in the diff, and no test pins it: `profile-compiler.test.ts` only checks `toContain('## Models')`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/ab198a038e01b94974c8d95973d27752fdb4a255/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L966-L968
findings.suggestion:
'relaunch or respawn after a gate rejection, a stall or a dead turn climbs one rung; a ' +
    'first CI fix round keeps its rung and a later one climbs one. A blocked task never climbs. ' +

findings.description: ADR 0090 still says `fixRoundRoute` climbs one rung for `ci-fix-round`, a reason the PR removed. The amendment marker corrects it, but rewording the first clause (e.g. "`fixRoundRoute` picks the rung for a fix round (decision 92)") would let the marker carry the whole claim.

`fixRoundFailure` keeps its own idea of which `respawn` events open a window (it drops undelivered round kickoffs before calling `windowFailure`). A new window-opening event would have to be added in both functions; one shared predicate would keep them in step.

`windowFailure` can no longer return `'repeat-fix-round'` (only `fixRoundFailure` does), yet its return type still allows it. Narrowing it, e.g. `Exclude<ClimbReason, 'repeat-fix-round'>`, would save callers from handling a value they never get.

The new `seedFinishedRound` helper appends the same `fix_round` / delivered `respawn` / `merge` sequence as `finishedRound` in `session-lifecycle.test.ts:1239-1248`. If `fixRoundFailure`'s event contract changes, both copies must change.

`fixRoundRoute`'s JSDoc partly restates the repeat-round and retry rules ("the retry of a killed one that failed") without naming which failures count. Pointing to `fixRoundFailure`'s doc instead would remove the duplicate, less precise copy.
`ClimbReason` is a literal union, but `docs/conventions/general.md` §Code layout asks for string enums for value sets. It predates this PR, which only swaps one member.
